newsitem.title: USA: US lobbyist alleges "shake down" for campaign cash.
newsitem.headline: US lobbyist alleges "shake down" for campaign cash.

text.p: An American lobbyist for the government of Pakistan complained last summer that he had been "shaken down" for campaign donations by Representative Dan Burton, the Republican now heading a House probe into alleged Democratic fund-raising abuses, the Washington Post reported on Wednesday.

Mark Siegel, then a lobbyist for the government of Prime Minister Benazir Bhutto, said he was approached by Burton early last year to raise "at least $5,000" for his re-election campaign, the newspaper said.

When he was unable to do so, Siegel said, the congressman complained to the then-ambassador for the Bhutto government in Washington and later threatened to make sure "none of his friends or colleagues" would meet with Siegel or his associates, the Post said.

"I should tell you," Siegel wrote July 25 in a two-page memo to a Bhutto aide in Islamabad, "that I worked in Washington for over 25 years and have never been shaken down by anyone before like Dan Burton's threats."
The Post said the memo was made available to the newspaper by a Democratic source in Congress and that Siegel, a longtime Democratic activist, confirmed its authenticity in an interview on Tuesday.

"No one has ever dared to threaten me into contributing money, and no one has ever followed through on such threats by contacting one of my clients," Siegel wrote. "Despite what you may see in the movies, this isn't the way most U.S. politicians conduct themselves."

The Post said Burton declined to be interviewed, but an aide told the newspaper that the congressman did talk to Siegel about raising campaign funds and conceded that he had spoken to the Pakistani ambassador about the matter.
But the aide said Siegel's memo was "full of egregious exaggerations and untruths" and took issue with most of the quotes attributed to Burton.
As chairman of the House Government Reform and Oversight Committee, Burton is heading the investigation of alleged fund-raising abuses in last year's election campaigns.
He also is a longtime member of the House International Relations Committee and co-chairs an informal caucus on U.S.-Pakistani relations.
